mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar rising-rate regimes, or the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS change shows no monotonicity.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate investment plans, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS up and UNRATE down.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates improved supply conditions without price pressure, prompting market expectations of sustained growth and a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >3% while CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day periods with similar INDPRO/CPIAUCSL shifts, SPX returns are negative or flat (mean return < 0.1%).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the goods price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months suggests persistent deflationary pressure, which reduces expected profit margins and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20 such deflationary months, SPX 5-day forward returns average positive (mean > 0.05%).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, the market anticipates tighter policy and reduces growth expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In regimes with similar FEDFUNDS MA thresholds, >50% of 20-day windows show non-negative SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) of over 100,000 jobs without a corresponding rise in CPIAUCSL suggests strong demand that boosts earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 100,000 for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < previous month
failure_condition: Over 60 days, SPX 60-day returns are negative in >40% of similar labor expansion events (p-value < 0.1 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the goods price index (CPIAUCSL) followed by a rebound above the prior month's level indicates easing price pressures, which can reduce uncertainty and support positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops by >1% in a month then rises by >0.5% in the following month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows with similar CPIAUCSL volatility, SPX returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for two consecutive months, the market interprets low rates as accommodative, boosting risk asset valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 60-day periods with similar FEDFUNDS behavior, SPX 60-day returns average negative (mean < 0.05%).
